summary: Some women do not drink the sotah water and do not get their kesubah: an arusah, a woman waiting for yibum, and women in a marriage that the Torah does not allow.

chunks.en: An arusah and a woman waiting for yibum
chunks.st: a betrothed woman who secluded herself with another man after being warned by her betrothed, and a widow waiting for her brother-in-law [yavam]
chunks.stMore: to perform levirate marriage who secluded herself with another man after being warned by her yavam,

words.note: Arusah: after kiddushin, before the chuppah.
Her late husband's brother, who may marry her through yibum.

chunks.en: do not drink, and do not get their kesubah,
chunks.st: they neither drink the bitter water nor collect payment of their marriage contracts.
chunks.stMore: The reason they are not entitled to payment of their marriage contracts is that the betrothed woman became forbidden to her betrothed or the widow became forbidden to her yavam due to her own actions of entering into seclusion with the paramour. And the fact that they do not drink the bitter water is

chunks.en: as the pasuk says,
chunks.st: as it is stated: “This is the law of jealousy,

chunks.en: "When a wife goes astray while under her husband,"
chunks.st: when a wife, while under her husband, goes astray, and is defiled” (Numbers 5:29).

chunks.en: leaving out an arusah and one waiting for yibum.
chunks.st: The verse excludes a betrothed woman and a widow awaiting her yavam;
chunks.stMore: since they are not yet married, neither is considered as “under her husband.” The mishna delineates cases where the woman’s marriage was prohibited in the first place: With regard to

chunks.en: A widow married to a Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: a widow who was married to a High Priest,

chunks.en: a divorced woman or a chalutzah married to a regular Kohen,
chunks.st: or a divorcée or ḥalutza who was married to a common priest,

words.note: A woman freed from yibum by chalitzah.

chunks.en: a mamzeres or a nesinah married to a Yisrael,
chunks.st: or a mamzeret or Gibeonite woman who was married to a Jew of unflawed lineage,

words.note: A girl born from a forbidden relationship.
A girl from the Givonim, who joined Klal Yisrael in Yehoshua's time.

chunks.en: or a Yisrael woman married to a mamzer or a nasin:
chunks.st: or a Jewish woman of unflawed lineage who was married to a mamzer or a Gibeonite,

chunks.en: they do not drink and do not get their kesubah.
chunks.st: all of these women neither drink the bitter water nor collect payment of their marriage contracts,
chunks.stMore: as the sota ritual applies only to permitted marriages.

summary: More women who do not drink: some lose their kesubah, and some still get it because it is their husband's doing. Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about a woman whose husband died first.

chunks.he: וְאֵלּוּ לֹא שׁוֹתוֹת וְלֹא נוֹטְלוֹת כְּתֻבָּה.
chunks.en: And these women do not drink and do not get their kesubah:
chunks.st: And the following women neither drink the bitter water nor collect payment of their marriage contracts:

chunks.en: one who says, "I am tamei,"
chunks.st: A woman who confesses and says: I am defiled,

chunks.en: and when witnesses came about her that she is tamei,
chunks.st: and a woman with regard to whom witnesses came and testified that she is defiled,

chunks.en: and one who says, "I will not drink."
chunks.st: and a woman who says: I will not drink
chunks.stMore: the bitter water, even if she does not confess her guilt.

chunks.en: If her husband said, "I will not make her drink,"
chunks.st: However, a woman whose husband said: I will not have her drink,

chunks.en: or her husband was with her as her husband on the way,
chunks.st: and a woman whose husband engaged in sexual intercourse with her on the way to the Temple,

chunks.en: she gets her kesubah and does not drink.
chunks.st: collect payment of their marriage contracts even though they do not drink
chunks.stMore: the bitter water, as it is due to the husbands that they do not drink.

chunks.en: If their husbands died before they drank,
chunks.st: If the husbands of sota women died before their wives drank the bitter water,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: They get their kesubah and do not drink.
chunks.st: They collect payment of their marriage contracts and they do not drink the bitter water.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: They do not drink, and they do not get their kesubah.
chunks.st: They either drink the bitter water or they do not collect payment of their marriage contracts.

summary: Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue about a woman who married while expecting or nursing another man's baby, and Rabbi Eliezer argues about a woman who cannot have children. All other women either drink or lose their kesubah.

chunks.en: A woman expecting another man's baby, or nursing another man's baby,
chunks.st: A woman who was pregnant with the child of another man at the time of her marriage and a woman who was nursing the child of another man at the time of her marriage

chunks.en: does not drink and does not get her kesubah.
chunks.st: neither drink the bitter water nor collect payment of their marriage contracts.
chunks.stMore: This is because by rabbinic law they may not marry for twenty-four months after the baby’s birth, and therefore these also constitute prohibited marriages.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: יָכוֹל הוּא לְהַפְרִישָׁהּ וּלְהַחֲזִירָהּ לְאַחַר זְמַן.
chunks.en: He can separate from her and take her back after the time is over.
chunks.st: He can separate from her, and remarry her after the time
chunks.stMore: of twenty-four months has elapsed, and therefore these are considered permitted marriages, and the women can drink the bitter water.

chunks.en: An aylonis, an old woman, and a woman who cannot have children
chunks.st: A sexually underdeveloped woman who is incapable of bearing children [ailonit], and an elderly woman, and a woman who is incapable of giving birth for other reasons,

words.note: A woman who cannot have children.

chunks.en: do not drink and do not get their kesubah.
chunks.st: neither collect payment of their marriage contracts nor drink
chunks.stMore: the bitter water, as marrying a woman who cannot give birth constitutes a violation of the mitzva to be fruitful and multiply.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:

chunks.en: He can marry another woman
chunks.st: He can marry another woman

chunks.en: and have children with her.
chunks.st: and procreate through her;
chunks.stMore: therefore, these are considered permitted marriages, and women in these categories can drink the bitter water.

chunks.en: And all other women
chunks.st: And all other women

chunks.he: אוֹ שׁוֹתוֹת אוֹ לֹא נוֹטְלוֹת כְּתֻבָּה:
chunks.en: either drink, or do not get their kesubah.
chunks.st: either drink the bitter water or do not collect payment of their marriage contracts.

summary: A Kohen's wife and a saris's wife also drink. A husband may warn his wife about any man, even relatives, except for a young boy.
stIntro: The wife of a priest drinks, and if she is found to be innocent of adultery, she

chunks.en: A Kohen's wife drinks, and (if she is innocent) she is allowed to her husband.
chunks.st: is permitted to her husband.

chunks.en: The wife of a saris drinks.
chunks.st: The wife of a eunuch also drinks.

words.note: A man who cannot have children.

chunks.en: A husband may warn her about any man, even close relatives,
chunks.st: A husband can issue a warning to his wife forbidding her to seclude herself with any man, even with regard to all those men with whom relations are forbidden, e.g., her father or brother, with the

chunks.en: except for a young boy,
chunks.st: exception of a minor

chunks.en: and except for one who is not a man.
chunks.st: and of one who is not a man,
chunks.stMore: i.e., in a situation where a man suspects his wife of bestiality.

summary: When a husband cannot warn his wife (he became deaf, lost his mind, or is in jail), beis din warns her. Rabbi Yosei says she can even be made to drink later.

chunks.en: And these are the women whom beis din warns:
chunks.st: And these are the women to whom the court issues a warning in place of their husbands:

words.note: Beis din, a court of Torah judges.

chunks.en: a woman whose husband became deaf or lost his mind,
chunks.st: One whose husband became a deaf-mute or became an imbecile,

chunks.en: or was locked up in jail.
chunks.st: or was incarcerated in prison.

chunks.en: They did not say this to make her drink,
chunks.st: The Sages said that the court warns her not in order to have her drink the bitter water if she disobeys the warning,

chunks.en: but to make her lose her kesubah.
chunks.st: but in order to disqualify her from receiving payment of her marriage contract.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says: The court’s warning

chunks.en: Also to make her drink:
chunks.st: also serves to have her drink,

chunks.en: when her husband gets out of jail, he makes her drink.
chunks.st: and when her husband is released from prison he has her drink.
